wouldHaveApproved: NO. Even absent the two outstanding items (the tester's held A5 iii/iv smoke steps and the LEGION-21 rebase), this head would not have been approved: finding B1 makes the merge queue unable to merge any template-conformant pull request, and finding B2 loses the recorded controller transcript on a reachable path the specification's Errors table covers. The eight should-fix findings are correctness gaps the specification did not anticipate; I would want them landed before approving as well, because each one strands or misdirects the very interactive controller and merge queue this change introduces.
verdictSummary: REQUEST_CHANGES: 2 blocking, 8 should-fix (one split across two comments), 2 informational comments, 1 batched fast-follow list (7 nits). Every finding is an inline review comment on the pull request naming file, line, clause, and expectation.

findings.clause: Spec Requirements: 'PR-body ## Verification block complete at that head'; plan T9 step 4 parenthetical '(CI/Threads/E2E lines name that sha)' mis-stated which lines carry the sha
findings.finding: Gate 5 requires the Threads line to name the head sha; the worker-skill template (lines 189-201, untouched) has no sha on the Threads line, so a conformant PR body can never pass and the merge queue never merges.
findings.expected: Every line filled (no <placeholder>); CI and E2E lines name <sha>; Thermo line names <sha> unless docs-only; Threads line reports 0 unresolved.

findings.clause: Spec Errors: 'controller pane dead on probe -> ensureController respawns with --resume when a session file is recorded'; Spec Requirements: 'resurrection resumes the recorded session file'; plan C1
findings.finding: retireAndRespawnStuckController's controllerAlive() probe (line 1673) deletes the locator with its ompSessionFile when the pane is dead; the `if (!stillAlive) return;` then leaves nothing for the next ensureController, which starts fresh and logs 'no OMP session file is recorded' (false).
findings.expected: Preferred: make controllerAlive() a pure probe and clear the locator in ensureController's dead branch right before spawnController (the root probe/removeTreeWindow split), removing the line-1401 snapshot. Alternative: respawn from this path with locator.ompSessionFile. Add a test where the stuck pane reads dead on the deadline probe and the respawn carries --resume=<file>.

findings.clause: Spec Design (extension): 'claimController sends ompSessionFile'; Spec Rejected: 'Controller restarts fresh on resurrection: loses the live conversation'; plan D2 covers only the no-locator case
findings.finding: An interactive takeover (/legion-claim-controller from a hand-started session) overwrites the daemon pane's recorded transcript with the operator's; a later respawn would --resume a file another live OMP process owns.
findings.expected: Send ompSessionFile only from claimController's session_start (daemon pane) path, not the slash-command path; test the slash-command body without the field.

findings.clause: Spec Requirements: controller is an interactive session Sami types into; Acceptance 3: claimed controller bash calls are wrapped
findings.finding: No session_switch/session_branch handling for the controller process: /new, /resume, /fork typed into the pane leave controllerSessionID stale (bash unwrapped, legion gh fails), never re-post /controller/ready (stale transcript), and on /new drop the Envoy role while the daemon trusts its stale state.roles record (every wake 404s until the pane dies).
findings.expected: Register session_switch/session_branch handlers that re-run claimController(context) for LEGION_CONTROLLER=1; test the switched session id is wrapped and /controller/ready re-posted. Daemon-side stale-role trust is a pre-existing gap for a follow-up.

findings.clause: Plan D1 ('recorded-but-missing session file throws, same-agent invariant, same as roots/workers'); packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md line 46 ('exactly as for roots and workers'); CLAUDE.md 'No silent fallbacks'
findings.finding: The missing-file refusal is one-shot and uncounted: the probe already dropped the locator, so the next call starts fresh with a misleading info log; mintControllerCapability rotates the hash before the throw. Roots count launchFailures and escalate; the controller does neither.
findings.expected: One consistent behaviour, documented: recommended an explicit error-level 'recorded transcript missing, starting fresh' without throwing and minting the capability after the resume decision; or D1's invariant with a launch-failure counter and ceiling and a transcript that survives the failed attempt.

findings.clause: Spec Requirements: controller merges only after live GitHub verification
findings.finding: gh pr view <n> / gh pr merge <n> / gh run rerun run from <state_dir>/controller, not a git checkout, so a bare number fails with 'not a git repository'.
findings.expected: Use <pr url> from the READY in place of <n>; give gh run rerun and the GraphQL query --repo <owner>/<repo> from that URL.

findings.finding: statusCheckRollup does not say which checks are required; as written the controller treats every check as required or guesses.
findings.expected: Name `legion gh -- pr checks <pr url> --required --json name,state,bucket` and define green (bucket pass; pending not green; fail never merges), or state the stricter every-check rule explicitly.

findings.clause: Plan D5 (controller resolves the architect topic from legion state --json); contracts roleToken lower-cases the Dispatch project part; the section's own 'Never hand-format a token'
findings.finding: Templates `legion-<project>-<KEY>-merger` / `legion-<project>-<root>-architect` splice the uppercase key in verbatim; such tokens never match a live role, so failed-gate reports and READY-republish requests are dropped or 404.
findings.expected: Read the exact token from the `roles` keys of `legion state --json` (root architects and phase workers are all present with role and issue); drop the templates or state the encoding (project token as printed, key lower-cased, role).

findings.clause: Spec Acceptance 3 / Errors: a claimed controller session's bash call is wrapped with LEGION_GRANT and the gh shim
findings.finding: The interactive-takeover instructions list only LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET(_FILE) and LEGION_DAEMON_URL; wrapBashWithGrant requires LEGION_STATE_DIR and blocks every bash call without it. Regression from pass-through.
findings.expected: Add LEGION_STATE_DIR to the takeover environment (or pass through with a one-time notify when unset); skill and code must agree.

findings.clause: Plan D5 READY shape `READY #<n> at <sha> for <KEY> (<pr url>)`; constraint A permits editing the merger bullet
findings.finding: Both give the short form `READY #<n> at <sha>`; merger.md and the controller skill define the long form and the controller depends on <KEY> and <pr url>.
findings.expected: Use the full shape in both places.

findings.clause: Plan T3 step 3 / processes.ts line 2673 comment: a /controller/ready that omits the field must not lose the recorded file
findings.finding: The omitted-field case is only tested against a locator that never had a file; an unconditional overwrite would pass.
findings.expected: Add a valid ready without ompSessionFile after withFile and assert /tmp/controller.jsonl survives.

observationsNotPostedToGitHub: Trust posture (pre-existing, not this change): the controller secret file <state_dir>/secrets/legion-<project>-controller is 0600 to the same unix user every worker pane runs as, so 'only the controller may merge' is a cooperative gate against well-behaved agents, not a capability boundary against a hostile worker — the same posture the boot tokens already have. Recorded here so nobody reads the spec's 'checked server-side' as stronger than it is.

Pre-existing hazard (not this change): controllerAlive() deletes whatever state.controllerLocator currently is after its own await, not only the locator it captured; a probe straddling a completed respawn would drop the new locator. Fixing B2 by making the probe pure also removes this.
The .omp/config.yml in the workspace working copy is the extension-provisioned file the gotchas doc says never to commit; review.json was committed with an explicit jj split path.
